## Overview

Distinguish native Messages, Chat Completions, and Completions traffic in inference metrics and traces, including requests without tools.

## Claims

- Add opt-in `api_surface` labels to existing request counts, latency histograms, token counters, and request token histograms through `--enable-api-surface-metrics` (disabled by default).
- Preserve the original metric schema and aggregate accounting unless enabled. Inference trace attribution remains independent of this setting.
- Preserve API identity through Messages conversion, parallel sampling, beam search, and streaming input.
- Cover native JSON/SSE endpoint attribution and document metric-query changes.

## Validation

656 focused CPU/unit tests passed across CLI/configuration, serving/conversion, engine admission, output processing, in-memory OTel export, metrics, beam search, and streaming input. All applicable full-branch pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.

Live validation on one NVIDIA H200 passed:

- 15 text-serving metric tests covering all three APIs in JSON/SSE with the flag disabled and enabled, plus existing default/chunked-prefill/hidden metric count checks.
- Two offline engine metric cases with n-gram speculative decoding, with the flag disabled and enabled.
- Six live OTLP requests with the metrics flag disabled, verifying `api_surface` on inference spans and preservation of incoming W3C trace IDs for all three APIs in JSON/SSE.

Validation used the complete candidate source on base `cffc0cfa31`, overlaid on compiled components from the October 16 nightly (`49cb2bbf71`, Torch `2.14.0+cu130`). The image has an extra MoE activation binding and an older tokenspeed-mla dependency compared with the base; neither is used by the validation models. This validates frontend behavior with precompiled components rather than an exact source-built binary.

Text serving used TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat with bfloat16, eager execution, and context 1024. Offline metrics used OPT-125m. Existing Buildkite suites cover the serving and metric tests; multimodal attribution cases are explicitly skipped.

<details>
<summary>Representative reproduction commands</summary>

```sh
# 44 metric unit cases
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/metrics \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_histogram_buckets.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_metrics_reader.py -q

# 117 CLI cases
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/engine \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -q

# 15 GPU serving cases
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_metrics.py \
  -k 'text and test_metrics_counts' -q

# Two GPU offline/speculative metric cases
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/engine/test_llm_engine.py \
  -k test_engine_metrics -q
```

Local CPU checks use `--confcutdir` to exclude the global accelerator-cleanup fixture, which fails in the local macOS PyTorch environment.

</details>

The OTLP smoke script exited successfully. Its abort-mode fixture shutdown logged an existing semaphore/zombie warning after assertions passed and GPU memory was released.

Ray, downstream product-image acceptance, and performance comparisons were not run. This change does not alter model weights or sampling; no accuracy or throughput improvement is claimed.

## Details

Messages reuses the Chat serving path internally, which previously prevented general engine telemetry from identifying the originating API. Carry trusted frontend identity into request/iteration statistics and reuse existing metric collectors and inference spans.

With `--enable-api-surface-metrics`, selected metric families receive one of four bounded values: `messages`, `chat_completions`, `completions`, or `unknown` for other/offline callers.

Default startup preserves the original labels and aggregate counters. Enabling the flag replaces selected aggregate series with per-API series; it does not export both copies. Before enabling it, update dashboard aggregations and vector joins as needed, using `sum without (api_surface)` for totals across APIs. Changing the setting requires a restart and increases series cardinality.

Scheduler gauges, the iteration histogram, and admission-time cache-tier counters remain engine-wide. Metric names, buckets, and engine-request counting semantics are preserved. Trace attribution works independently of the metrics flag.

This differs from [#61571](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61571), which currently focuses on tool-specific outcome metrics, and [#52249](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52249), whose operation label does not distinguish Messages. Neither is a dependency; reconcile overlapping identity plumbing if either merges first. Render-server instrumentation is outside this change.

@@ -37,6 +37,85 @@ The following metrics are exposed:
 
 --8<-- "gen:metrics-general"
 
+### API attribution
+
+By default, request metrics retain their existing labels and aggregate traffic
+across APIs. To distinguish Messages, Chat Completions, and Completions traffic,
+start the server with `--enable-api-surface-metrics`:
+
+```console
+vllm serve <model> --enable-api-surface-metrics
+```
+
+This opt-in setting adds an `api_surface` label to the following request metrics:
+
+- `vllm:request_success_total` (with the existing `finished_reason` label)
+- `vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds`
+- `vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds`
+- `vllm:request_time_per_output_token_seconds`
+- `vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds`
+- `vllm:request_queue_time_seconds`
+- `vllm:request_inference_time_seconds`
+- `vllm:request_prefill_time_seconds`
+- `vllm:request_decode_time_seconds`
+- `vllm:prompt_tokens_total`
+- `vllm:generation_tokens_total`
+- `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source_total` (with the existing `source` label)
+- `vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_total`
+- `vllm:request_prompt_tokens`
+- `vllm:request_generation_tokens`
+- `vllm:request_prefill_kv_computed_tokens`
+
+Its values are `messages` for `/v1/messages`, `chat_completions` for
+`/v1/chat/completions`, `completions` for `/v1/completions`, and `unknown`
+for callers without one of these API identities, including offline generation
+and Cohere requests.
+When enabled, the label applies to streaming and non-streaming generation,
+including requests without tools, and does not require tracing. See the
+[OpenTelemetry guide](../../examples/observability/opentelemetry/README.md#api-attribution)
+for trace attribution.
+
+Histogram buckets and counting semantics are unchanged. These metrics describe
+engine requests: multiple generated choices contribute separately, and errors
+rejected before engine admission are excluded. Enabling the setting replaces
+the aggregate series with four sets of series per model and engine, one per API
+value; it does not export both aggregate and per-API copies. Disabling it restores
+the original labels. Changing the setting requires a server restart.
+
+Token counters update as engine outputs arrive, including before a request
+finishes. Prompt tokens are counted at prefill completion, with their existing
+local-compute, local-cache, and external-transfer breakdown. Generation tokens
+count all emitted token IDs, including multiple tokens in one engine output.
+The scheduler's `vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_by_source_total` counter tracks
+cache-tier hits at admission and remains engine-wide, as do scheduler gauges
+and the per-iteration token histogram.
+
+For example, request throughput by API can be queried with:
+
+```promql
+sum by (api_surface) (rate(vllm:request_success_total[5m]))
+```
+
+For output token throughput by API:
+
+```promql
+sum by (api_surface) (rate(vllm:generation_tokens_total[5m]))
+```
+
+To query p95 end-to-end latency by API:
+
+```promql
+histogram_quantile(0.95,
+  sum by (api_surface, le) (rate(vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))
+```
+
+Before enabling the setting, update dashboard aggregations and vector joins
+that assume a single series per model, engine, and finish reason. For totals
+across APIs, aggregate with `sum without (api_surface)`. Each label combination
+adds series, including histogram buckets, so account for the increased scrape
+and storage volume. Existing queries retain their original behavior while the
+setting remains disabled.
+
